fields.label: Holidays and Your Special Needs Child – Tips to Avoid Holiday Stress

fields.value: With all its magic, the holiday season has a way of becoming overly busy, even in the best of circumstances. Every year, we try to pace ourselves and remain focused on what matters most: time with loved ones, creating meaningful memories, and getting the break we need to “reset” for a new year.

fields.value: The silver lining this time, when the risk of novel coronavirus transmission will keep many of us out of public places and large gatherings, is a chance to reimagine traditions that can maximize the joys of the season and minimize the holiday stress.

fields.value: Here are some helpful tips to make the most of your special time together.

fields.value: With a special needs child, keep it simple!
fields.label: With a special needs child, keep it simple!

fields.value: 2020 has been the year of a “new normal,” so everyone understands the need to modify family celebrations to fit your current lifestyle. From shopping to decorating, some traditions of the past may seem impossible to accomplish now. Scaling back and creating your own mix of old and new holiday traditions, and asking all of your children for input, can be a great way to reconnect and refocus the season on the family fun, memories, and joy of giving that matter most.

fields.value: Prepare your family for the holiday season

fields.value: Once you have some plans for the holidays, take time to make the whole family as happy and comfortable with your agenda as possible. Informal daily briefings during mealtimes, for example, are one way to discuss what is going to happen and what to pack for maximum comfort. Color-coded calendars can visually remind children of plans and help them focus on what they can do to contribute. fields.value: Holidays and Your Special Needs Child – Tips to Avoid Holiday Stress
fields.label: Holidays and Your Special Needs Child – Tips to Avoid Holiday Stress

fields.value: With all its magic, the holiday season has a way of becoming overly busy, even in the best of circumstances. Every year, we try to pace ourselves and remain focused on what matters most: time with loved ones, creating meaningful memories, and getting the break we need to “reset” for a new year.
fields.label: With all its magic, the holiday season has a way of becoming overly busy, even in the best

fields.value: The silver lining this time, when the risk of novel coronavirus transmission will keep many of us out of public places and large gatherings, is a chance to reimagine traditions that can maximize the joys of the season and minimize the holiday stress.
fields.label: The silver lining this time, when the risk of novel coronavirus transmission will keep man

fields.value: Here are some helpful tips to make the most of your special time together.
fields.label: Here are some helpful tips to make the most of your special time together.

fields.value: With a special needs child, keep it simple!
fields.label: With a special needs child, keep it simple!

fields.value: 2020 has been the year of a “new normal,” so everyone understands the need to modify family celebrations to fit your current lifestyle. From shopping to decorating, some traditions of the past may seem impossible to accomplish now. Scaling back and creating your own mix of old and new holiday traditions, and asking all of your children for input, can be a great way to reconnect and refocus the season on the family fun, memories, and joy of giving that matter most.
fields.label: 2020 has been the year of a “new normal,” so everyone understands the need to modify famil

fields.value: Invitations abound this time of year. Choose to do what works for you and your family, and do not feel guilty about saying, “No, thank you” to lower priorities.
fields.label: Invitations abound this time of year. Choose to do what works for you and your family, and

fields.value: Prepare your family for the holiday season
fields.label: Prepare your family for the holiday season

fields.value: Once you have some plans for the holidays, take time to make the whole family as happy and comfortable with your agenda as possible. Informal daily briefings during mealtimes, for example, are one way to discuss what is going to happen and what to pack for maximum comfort. Color-coded calendars can visually remind children of plans and help them focus on what they can do to contribute. Photos of friends and family, with or without masks, can get children ready for the faces they will see. If a video gathering is coming up, practice among yourselves ahead of time.

fields.label: Holidays and Your Special Needs Child – Tips to Avoid Holiday Stress

fields.value: With all its magic, the holiday season has a way of becoming overly busy, even in the best of circumstances. Every year, we try to pace ourselves and remain focused on what matters most: time with loved ones, creating meaningful memories, and getting the break we need to “reset” for a new year.

fields.value: The silver lining this time, when the risk of novel coronavirus transmission will keep many of us out of public places and large gatherings, is a chance to reimagine traditions that can maximize the joys of the season and minimize the holiday stress.

fields.value: Here are some helpful tips to make the most of your special time together.
fields.label: Here are some helpful tips to make the most of your special time together.

fields.value: With a special needs child, keep it simple!
fields.label: With a special needs child, keep it simple!

fields.value: 2020 has been the year of a “new normal,” so everyone understands the need to modify family celebrations to fit your current lifestyle. From shopping to decorating, some traditions of the past may seem impossible to accomplish now. Scaling back and creating your own mix of old and new holiday traditions, and asking all of your children for input, can be a great way to reconnect and refocus the season on the family fun, memories, and joy of giving that matter most.

fields.value: Prepare your family for the holiday season
fields.label: Prepare your family for the holiday season

fields.value: Once you have some plans for the holidays, take time to make the whole family as happy and comfortable with your agenda as possible. Informal daily briefings during mealtimes, for example, are one way to discuss what is going to happen and what to pack for maximum comfort. Color-coded calendars can visually remind children of plans and help them focus on what they can do to contribute. Photos of friends and family, with or without masks, can get children ready for the faces they will see. If a video gathering is coming up, practice among yourselves ahead of time.

fields.label: Holidays and Your Special Needs Child – Tips to Avoid Holiday Stress

fields.value: With all its magic, the holiday season has a way of becoming overly busy, even in the best of circumstances. Every year, we try to pace ourselves and remain focused on what matters most: time with loved ones, creating meaningful memories, and getting the break we need to “reset” for a new year.
fields.label: With all its magic, the holiday season has a way of becoming overly busy, even in the best

fields.value: The silver lining this time, when the risk of novel coronavirus transmission will keep many of us out of public places and large gatherings, is a chance to reimagine traditions that can maximize the joys of the season and minimize the holiday stress.
fields.label: The silver lining this time, when the risk of novel coronavirus transmission will keep man

fields.value: Here are some helpful tips to make the most of your special time together.
fields.label: Here are some helpful tips to make the most of your special time together.

fields.value: With a special needs child, keep it simple!
fields.label: With a special needs child, keep it simple!

fields.value: 2020 has been the year of a “new normal,” so everyone understands the need to modify family celebrations to fit your current lifestyle. From shopping to decorating, some traditions of the past may seem impossible to accomplish now. Scaling back and creating your own mix of old and new holiday traditions, and asking all of your children for input, can be a great way to reconnect and refocus the season on the family fun, memories, and joy of giving that matter most.

fields.value: Invitations abound this time of year. Choose to do what works for you and your family, and do not feel guilty about saying, “No, thank you” to lower priorities.

fields.value: Prepare your family for the holiday season
fields.label: Prepare your family for the holiday season

fields.value: Once you have some plans for the holidays, take time to make the whole family as happy and comfortable with your agenda as possible. Informal daily briefings during mealtimes, for example, are one way to discuss what is going to happen and what to pack for maximum comfort. Color-coded calendars can visually remind children of plans and help them focus on what they can do to contribute. Photos of friends and family, with or without masks, can get children ready for the faces they will see. If a video gathering is coming up, practice among yourselves ahead of time.

fields.label: Holidays and Your Special Needs Child – Tips to Avoid Holiday Stress

fields.value: With all its magic, the holiday season has a way of becoming overly busy, even in the best of circumstances. Every year, we try to pace ourselves and remain focused on what matters most: time with loved ones, creating meaningful memories, and getting the break we need to “reset” for a new year.

fields.value: 2020 has been the year of a “new normal,” so everyone understands the need to modify family celebrations to fit your current lifestyle. From shopping to decorating, some traditions of the past may seem impossible to accomplish now. Scaling back and creating your own mix of old and new holiday traditions, and asking all of your children for input, can be a great way to reconnect and refocus the season on the family fun, memories, and joy of giving that matter most.

fields.value: Once you have some plans for the holidays, take time to make the whole family as happy and comfortable with your agenda as possible. fields.value: 2020 has been the year of a “new normal,” so everyone understands the need to modify family celebrations to fit your current lifestyle. From shopping to decorating, some traditions of the past may seem impossible to accomplish now. Scaling back and creating your own mix of old and new holiday traditions, and asking all of your children for input, can be a great way to reconnect and refocus the season on the family fun, memories, and joy of giving that matter most.

fields.value: Once you have some plans for the holidays, take time to make the whole family as happy and comfortable with your agenda as possible. Informal daily briefings during mealtimes, for example, are one way to discuss what is going to happen and what to pack for maximum comfort. Color-coded calendars can visually remind children of plans and help them focus on what they can do to contribute. Photos of friends and family, with or without masks, can get children ready for the faces they will see. If a video gathering is coming up, practice among yourselves ahead of time.
